Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.summary: A fungal disease (Puccinia sorghi) causing reddish-brown, elongated pustules on both leaf surfaces. Rarely causes major yield loss in resistant hybrids but can be more damaging in cool, humid conditions.
care_tips: Favor planting resistant or tolerant corn varieties where available.
Monitor fields regularly, especially during cool, humid weather.
Fungicide treatment is generally only warranted if pustules appear early and are widespread, particularly on susceptible sweet corn.
Avoid dense planting to help leaves dry faster after rain or dew.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.disclaimer: For fungicide selection and timing, consult your local agricultural extension office.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: A viral disease spread by whiteflies, causing stunted growth, small yellowing leaves that curl upward, and reduced fruit production. There is no cure once a plant is infected.
care_tips: Prevention is the only effective strategy — infected plants cannot be cured.
Choose TYLCV-resistant tomato varieties when planting.
Control whitefly populations with sticky traps and by inspecting new transplants before planting.
Remove and discard infected plants promptly to reduce spread to healthy plants.
Reflective mulch can help reduce whitefly landing on plants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.disclaimer: This is a viral disease with no chemical cure; management focuses entirely on prevention and vector control.

Tomato___Early_blight.title: Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.summary: A common fungal disease (Alternaria) causing brown spots with concentric rings on older, lower leaves first. Can spread to stems and fruit, reducing yield if left unmanaged.
care_tips: Water at the base of the plant rather than overhead, to keep foliage dry.
Add mulch around the base of plants to reduce soil splashing onto leaves.
Stake or cage plants and remove lower leaves to improve airflow.
Rotate tomato planting locations, avoiding the same spot for at least two years.
Remove and dispose of infected leaves rather than composting them in a home pile unless hot-composting.
Tomato___Early_blight.disclaimer: For fungicide options, consult your local agricultural extension office.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.summary: A fungal disease (Exserohilum turcicum) producing long, cigar-shaped gray-to-tan lesions on leaves. Can cause significant yield loss if it develops before tasseling in susceptible plants.
care_tips: Choose resistant corn hybrids where available — this is the most effective management approach.
Rotate away from corn for at least one growing season to reduce fungal spores surviving in residue.
Till or plow under crop debris after harvest to speed decomposition of infected material.
Scout fields regularly, especially during warm, humid weather with extended leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.disclaimer: For fungicide recommendations, consult your local agricultural extension office, as effectiveness varies by region and hybrid susceptibility.

Strawberry.title: Strawberry — General Care
Strawberry.summary: This plant was identified at the species level; a specific disease could not be determined. General growing guidance is provided below.
care_tips: Plant in full sun, ideally at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight per day.
Use well-drained, sandy loam soil rich in organic matter, with a pH around 6.0-6.5.
Water at the base of plants, providing about 1-1.5 inches of water per week during key growth stages.
Apply a layer of straw mulch to conserve moisture, keep berries clean, and reduce disease spread.
Avoid planting where tomatoes, peppers, eggplant, or potatoes have grown in the past few years, as they can carry diseases that also affect strawberries.
Strawberry.disclaimer: This app does not diagnose a specific disease for this species. If you notice unusual spots, wilting, or discoloration, consult a local extension office or nursery.

Blueberry.title: Blueberry — General Care
Blueberry.summary: This plant was identified at the species level; a specific disease could not be determined. General growing guidance is provided below.
care_tips: Plant in full sun, at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily.
Blueberries require acidic soil, ideally a pH between 4.5 and 5.5 — a soil test is recommended before planting.
Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged; blueberries have shallow roots sensitive to both drought and standing water.
Water at the base of the plant in the morning rather than overhead, to reduce the risk of fungal disease on wet foliage.
Mulch with an acidic material such as pine needles or pine bark to help retain moisture and maintain soil pH.
Blueberry.disclaimer: This app does not diagnose a specific disease for this species. If you notice unusual spots, wilting, or discoloration, consult a local extension office or nursery.
